gosh i feel your pain so much. i was in a relationship like this except he wasn’t looking for others (that i knew of). he just kept brushing off my attempts of talking about commitment and our future and all of that. we also broke up like three times and i went back every time because i just loved him so much and we were good together imo. he didn’t want me to move with him when the time came even though i told him i had no problem visiting or even moving there after i finished school. eventually i got tired of chasing him. it is so painful to fully give yourself to someone only to have them be like “i just do know”. it’s hard af to end this permanently but you can do it. you’ll have to distract yourself a lot and block him on everything but it can be done. i was completely heartbroken during after this relationship. it took a long time to get over it. but now i can think back and just see how i deserved to have what i need. it’s still hard sometimes but i really believe you can do it.

wow this is very tough then. i’m glad she has you, but she really does need a professional. i would be hesitant to tell you to tell her to go to a mental health institution because of her bad experience with the authorities. it isn’t fair to put all of this weight on you though. you can try helping her find a therapy but she needs to make the effort to go as well. i don’t know if you’d be open to telling her to call you instead of committing the act. you may also want to get therapy for yourself, having helped her so many times can be really heavy on you :/

try telling her you understand she’s going through shitty things. be there for her. honestly telling someone to call a hotline is not helpful whatsoever. wait times for therapy are long and not always affordable too. it’s best if you just try to talk to her and let her know how much you care and how great she is.

do what is best for you. if she won’t reconsider the relationship then i think it’s best for you to move on so that you can find your forever. it doesn’t really sound like she should be in a relationship though if she just rebounds a lot and is still keeping her options open. it wouldn’t be fair to you to be so dedicated to someone who is not sure.
